newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cartel office approves Munich Re's DKV takeover.
newsitem.headline: Cartel office approves Munich Re's DKV takeover.

text.p: Germany's cartel office said on Tuesday that it had approved Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG's plan to take over 51 percent of Deutsche Krankenversicherungs AG from Allianz AG Holding.

The takeover of Germany's leading health insurer was agreed in a complex share swap between Munich Re and Allianz earlier this year which enabled Allianz to take full control of the Vereinte health insurance group.

The approval was effectively a formality after the cartel office said earlier it had approved Allianz's plan to take over Vereinte, the second largest German health insurance company and Hermes, Germany's leading loan insurer.
Munich Re and Allianz arranged the deal which would give Munich Re control of DKV last July. Munich Re already owns 10 percent of DKV directly and 39 percent indirectly.
Allianz in return would get Hermes, the 25 percent of Vereinte's health unit it did not already own and Munich Re's holding in its own Austrian activities.
Munich Re said on Monday that it planned to consolidate DKV in its group accounts in the current business year.
